1.pericope_label: Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?
debates: Under which Darius the prophecy was spoken
How a comparison could be made a week into the work
Why the twenty-first day of the month was chosen
outliers: Ellicott ties the message to the last day of the Feast of Tabernacles
Henry warns that praising the former age can expose the present one to contempt
Calvin says the earlier prophecies of a greater temple were themselves the temptation
themes: A harvest festival kept after a scanty harvest
Old men recalling gold and carved pillars
Foundations laid years before and left standing
A house its builders were calling a shed

4.pericope_label: Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith the LORD; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the LORD, and work: for I am with you
debates: Whether the word covenanted is the old promise or the personal Word
Whether the spirit meant is the Holy Spirit or the gift of prophecy
What the encouragement actually rests on
outliers: Gill identifies the word of the covenant with the Angel who went before them in the pillar
Ellicott records that the later Jews dated the departure of the Spirit to the last prophets
Clarke asks what the most splendid cathedral is worth without a messenger in it
themes: A day of small things nobody should despise
Presence counted as the real glory of a building
A promise older than the ruins being rebuilt
A pillar of cloud recalled at a building site

6.pericope_label: Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come
debates: Whether the desire of all nations is a person or the treasures of the nations
Whether the shaking is physical, political, or moral
How long a little while is allowed to be
outliers: Ellicott names unwillingness to lose a Messianic proof as the motive for the received rendering
Ellicott says the original must be read without deference to its use in a later argument
Clarke reports that no manuscript supports the emendation that would rescue the singular
themes: One epoch counted as a single short season
Earthquakes read as changes in the human heart
Gentile treasure carried into a poor building
A verse about silver left meaningless by the other reading

8.pericope_label: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts. The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the LORD of hosts: and in this place will I give peace
debates: Whether the silver and gold are disclaimed or promised
What the greater glory of the second house consists in
Whether the peace is a peace-offering or peace itself
outliers: Ellicott calls the reading that God needs no silver unnatural here
Clarke refuses to ground the greater glory in the presence of Christ, since Christ is equal to God and not greater
Gill lists the five things the second house was owned to lack
themes: A gift that only returns what was lent
A model drawn by the owner of the house
An ark and a fire that never came back
Peace first proclaimed in a poor building

10.pericope_label: Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Ask now the priests concerning the law, saying, If one bear holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with his skirt do touch bread... shall it be holy?
debates: What the two ritual questions are actually being used to prove
Why a prophet is sent to ask the priests for a ruling
Whether the point is the acceptability of sacrifice or the motive of the builders
outliers: Calvin says no interpreter has clearly expressed the passage and calls their accounts jejune and frigid
Ellicott notes the sharpest half of the argument is left for the hearers to supply
Henry has the prophet decline to take the ordinary minister’s work out of his hands
themes: Holiness that stops at the first touch
Uncleanness that travels as far as the sanctuary
A fine building mistaken for a finished duty
Industry that turns into superstition

13.pericope_label: Then said Haggai, If one that is unclean by a dead body touch any of these, shall it be unclean? And the priests answered and said, It shall be unclean
debates: Whether the reckoning runs backward over past years or forward from that day
What the vessel in the winepress clause actually is
Why the argument is pitched at food and drink
outliers: Calvin takes the disputed word as forward and rebuilds the whole passage as one long sentence
Calvin finds an indirect reproach in the prophet declining to announce deep mysteries
Ellicott traces the plagues to an older list and notes which one Haggai has added
themes: Holiness that will not travel, uncleanness that will
Ordinances polluted by the hands that bring them
A heap that yields half what it promised
Hail added to an old catalogue of curses

18.pericope_label: Consider now from this day and upward, from the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, even from the day that the foundation of the LORD’S temple was laid, consider it
debates: Whether the seed is still in the barn, already sown, or simply not there
Whether the clause reads from the day or to the day of the founding
What change the day itself marks
outliers: Ellicott calls the received rendering of the verse quite unintelligible
Gill argues the promise is the more remarkable for coming before any sign of the crop
Ellicott says the word for seed means grain for eating, not grain for sowing
themes: A promise made before any shoot is visible
Fifteen years of spasmodic and feeble effort
Empty barns at the end of a blighted season
A blessing dated from a particular morning

20.pericope_label: Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying, I will shake the heavens and the earth... In that day will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, and will make thee as a signet
debates: Which upheaval among the nations the shaking refers to
Whether the signet promise can be meant of the governor himself
Whether the shaking is God’s ordinary providence or one particular work
outliers: Calvin calls the reading that makes the shaking a continued act very frigid
Gill argues from the words in that day that the promise outruns the man addressed
Henry sets the ruler’s anxieties against the farmers’ as needing a separate sermon
themes: Two sermons on one day for two kinds of hearer
A world always moving and sometimes turbulent
Armies destroyed by each other’s swords
A ring kept carefully and never lent out
